==English== ===Pronunciation=== * {{enPR|gān}}, {{IPA|en|/ɡeɪn/}} * {{audio|en|en-us-gain.ogg|a=US}} * {{rhymes|en|eɪn|s=1}} ===Etymology 1=== From {{inh|en|enm|gayn|id=gain}}, {{m|enm|gain}}, {{m|enm|gein||profit, advantage}}, from {{der|en|non|gagn||benefit, advantage, use}}, from {{der|en|gem-pro|*gagną}}, {{m|gem-pro|*gaganą||gain, profit", literally "return}}, from {{der|en|gem-pro|*gagana||back, against, in return}}, a reduplication of {{der|en|gem-pro|*ga-||with, together}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*ḱóm||next to, at, with, along}}. Cognate with {{cog|is|gagn||gain, advantage, use}}, {{cog|sv|gagn||benefit, profit}}, {{cog|da|gavn||gain, profit, success}}, {{cog|got|𐌲𐌰𐌲𐌴𐌹𐌲𐌰𐌽||to gain, profit}}, {{cog|non|gegn||ready}}, dialectal {{cog|sv|gen||useful, noteful}}, {{cog|la|cum||with}}; see {{l|en|gain-}}, {{l|en|again}}, {{l|en|against}}. Compare also {{cog|enm|gaynen}}, {{m|enm|geinen||to be of use, profit, avail}}, {{cog|is|-}} and {{cog|sv|gagna||to avail, help}}, {{cog|da|gavne||to benefit}}. The Middle English word was reinforced by {{der|en|frm|gain||gain, profit, advancement, cultivation}}, from {{der|en|fro|gaaing}}, {{m|fro|gaaigne}}, {{m|fro|gaigne}}, a noun derivative of {{m|fro|gaaignier}}, {{m|fro|gaigner||to till, earn, win}}, from {{der|en|frk|*waiþanōn||to pasture, graze, hunt for food}}, ultimately from {{der|en|gem-pro|*waiþiz}}, {{m|gem-pro|*waiþō}}, {{m|gem-pro|*waiþijō||pasture, field, hunting ground}}; compare {{cog|goh|weidōn}}, {{m|goh|weidanōn||to hunt, forage for food}} (Modern {{cog|de|Weide||pasture}}), {{cog|non|veiða||to catch, hunt}}, {{cog|ang|wǣþan||to hunt, chase, pursue}}. Related to {{m|en|wide}}. ====Verb==== {{en-verb}} # {{lb|en|transitive}} To acquire [[possession]] of. #: {{ux|en|Looks like you’ve '''gained''' a new friend.}} #* {{RQ:KJV|Matthew|16|26||What is a man profited, if he shall '''gain''' the whole world, and lose his own soul?}} #* {{RQ:Tennyson In Memoriam|XXI|35|Another answers, ‘Let him be,
⁠He loves to make parade of pain,
⁠That with his piping he may '''gain'''
The praise that comes to constancy.’}} # {{lb|en|intransitive}} To have or receive advantage or profit; to acquire gain; to grow rich; to advance in interest, health, or happiness; to make progress. #: {{ux|en|The sick man '''gains''' daily.}} #* {{RQ:KJV|Ezekiel|22|12||Thou hast greedily '''gained''' of thy neighbours by extortion.}} # {{lb|en|transitive|dated}} To come off winner or victor in; to be successful in; to obtain by competition. #: {{co|en|to '''gain''' a battle; to '''gain''' a case at law}} # {{lb|en|transitive}} To [[increase]]. #* {{RQ:Pyle Robin Hood|chapter=V|passage=Then they had bouts of wrestling and of cudgel play, so that every day they '''gained''' in skill and strength.}} # {{lb|en|intransitive|often with {{m|en|on}}}} To grow more likely to catch or overtake someone. #: {{co|en|to [[gain ground|'''gain''' ground]]}} #: {{ux|en|I’m '''gaining''' (on you).}} # {{lb|en|transitive}} To [[reach]]. #: {{co|en|to '''gain''' the top of a mountain}} #* {{RQ:London Iron Heel|passage=Ernest laughed harshly and savagely when he had '''gained''' the street.}} # To draw into any interest or party; to win to one’s side; to conciliate. #* {{RQ:KJV|Matthew|18|15|passage=If he shall hear thee, thou hast '''gained''' thy brother.}} #* {{RQ:Dryden Aeneis|passage=to gratify the queen, and '''gain''' the court}} # {{lb|en|intransitive}} To [[put on weight]]. #: {{ux|en|I’ve been '''gaining'''.}} # {{senseid|en|fast}} {{lb|en|dated|ambitransitive|of a timekeeping device}} To run fast, often by a specified amount. #: {{ux|en|Don't rely on that clock: it '''gains'''.}} #* {{RQ:Bramah Bravo of London|passage="Don't hurry immediately after your breakfast, Geoffrey. You know that clock '''gains''' five minutes every day and it's only—" called out Miss Tilehurst, but Geoffrey was technically out of earshot then {{...}}}} =====Conjugation===== {{en-conj|old=1|past_old=gain'd}} =====Antonyms===== * {{antsense|to run slower than expected}} {{l|en|lose}} =====Derived terms===== {{col|en|gainable |gainer |gain ground |gain line |gain momentum |gain on |gain one's spurs |gain over |gain steam |gain the wind |gain time |gain traction |gain weight |outgain |overgain |undergain |ungained|gain upon |what you gain on the swings you lose on the roundabouts,what you lose on the swings you gain on the roundabouts }} =====Translations===== {{trans-top|acquire}} * Arabic: * Armenian: * Aromanian: * Bulgarian: * Chinese: * Dutch: * Finnish: * French: * Galician: * Georgian: * German: * Gothic: * Greek: * Hebrew: * Hungarian: * Interlingua: * Irish: * Italian: * Japanese: * Korean: * Latgalian: * Latin: * Latvian: * Middle English: * Polish: * Portuguese: * Romanian: * Russian: {{t+|ru|получа́ть|impf}}, {{t+|ru|получи́ть|pf}}, {{t+|ru|приобрета́ть}}, {{t+|ru|приобрести́}} * Sanskrit: * Spanish: * Swedish: * Telugu: * Ukrainian: {{trans-bottom}} {{trans-top|be more likely to catch}} * Swedish: {{trans-bottom}} {{trans-top|reach}} * Esperanto: * Irish: * Swedish: {{trans-bottom}} {{trans-top|put on weight}} * Bulgarian: * Dutch: * Galician: * Hungarian: * Irish: * Italian: * Polish: * Spanish: * Swedish: {{trans-bottom}} ====Noun==== {{en-noun|~}} # The act of gaining; [[acquisition]]. #: {{ux|en|People are more willing to [[take a risk]] to avoid a loss than to make a '''gain'''.}} #* {{RQ:Marlowe Tamburlaine|part=1|scene=ii|page=31|passage=All running headlong after greedie ſpoiles:

{{t+check|tr|kazanmak}} {{trans-bottom}} ===Etymology 2=== From dialectal English {{m|en|gen}}, {{m|en|gin}}, short for {{m|en|again}}, {{m|en|agen||against}}; also {{der|en|enm|gain}}, {{m|enm|gayn}}, {{m|enm|gein}}, {{m|enm|ȝæn||against}}, from {{der|en|ang|gēan}}, {{m|ang|geġn||against}}. More at {{l|en|against}}. ====Preposition==== {{en-head|prep}} # {{lb|en|obsolete}} [[against|Against]]. =====Derived terms===== *{{l|en|foregain}} * {{l|en|gainful}} ===Etymology 3=== From {{inh|en|enm|gayn|id=direct}}, {{m|enm|gein}}, {{m|enm|geyn||straight, direct, short, fit, good}}, from {{der|en|non|gegn||straight, direct, short, ready, serviceable, kindly}}, from {{m|non|gegn||pos=adverb|opposite, against}} (whence {{m|non|gagna||to go against, meet, suit, be meet}}); see above. Adverb from {{inh|en|enm|gayn}}, {{m|enm|gayne||fitly, quickly}}, from the adjective. ====Adjective==== {{en-adj}} # {{lb|en|obsolete|or|dialectal}} [[straight|Straight]], [[direct]]; [[near]]; [[short]]. #: {{co|en|the '''gainest''' way}} # {{lb|en|obsolete|or|dialectal}} [[suitable|Suitable]]; [[convenient]]; [[ready]]. # {{lb|en|dialectal}} [[easy|Easy]]; [[tolerable]]; [[handy]], [[dexterous]]. # {{lb|en|dialectal}} [[honest|Honest]]; [[respectable]]; [[moderate]]; [[cheap]]. =====Derived terms===== *{{l|en|gainand}} * {{l|en|gainly}} * {{l|en|gainsome}} *{{l|en|ungain}} =====Translations===== {{trans-top|straight, direct}} * Swedish: {{trans-bottom}} ====Adverb==== {{en-adv}} # {{lb|en|obsolete|or|dialectal}} [[straightly|Straightly]]; [[quickly]]; by the nearest way or means. # {{lb|en|dialectal}} [[suitably|Suitably]]; [[conveniently]]; [[dexterously]]; [[moderately]]. # {{lb|en|dialectal}} [[tolerably|Tolerably]]; [[fairly]]. #: {{coi|en|'''gain''' quiet|t=fairly/pretty quiet}} ===Etymology 4=== Compare {{cog|cy|gan||a mortise}}. ====Noun==== {{en-noun}} # {{lb|en|architecture}} A [[square]] or [[bevel]]led [[notch]] cut out of a [[girder]], [[bind]]ing [[joist]], or other [[timber]] which [[support]]s a [[floor]] [[beam]], so as to receive the end of the floor beam. ===Anagrams=== * {{anagrams|en|a=agin|Agin|Agni|Angi|Gina|NGIA|Nagi|Ngai|a- -ing|ag'in|agin|gina|inga}}
